key.name: resolution
key.description: Scale the captured video down to this size before encoding. "auto" lets the receiver's own limits decide, which is what Chrome does. Above 1080p, raise the bitrate to match and expect a hardware encoder to be needed for a smooth stream.

key.name: fps
key.description: Frames per second, or 0 to let the receiver's limits decide.

key.name: bitrate-kbps
key.description: Roughly 4000 for 720p, 8000 for 1080p, 16000 for 1440p and 30000 for 4K; more for fast-moving content. 0 lets the receiver's limits decide.

key.name: audio-bitrate-kbps
key.description: Opus bitrate for the cast audio, or 0 to let the receiver's limits decide.

key.name: video-encoder
key.description: Which encoder to use. "auto" prefers hardware (VA-API, NVENC, V4L2) and falls back to software. Choose software when a graphics driver produces a broken or stuttering picture. "vaapi" (Intel, AMD), "nvenc" (NVIDIA) and "v4l2" (Arm boards) pin one hardware API. Casting fails with a message if the choice cannot be met.

key.name: video-codec
key.description: Automatic lets the receiver choose from the available codecs

key.name: video-format
key.description: The raw video format handed to the encoder. "auto" offers both and lets negotiation pick whichever the chosen encoder accepts. Forcing a format restricts casting to encoders that accept it, which on most systems means forcing the encoder type too.

key.name: show-details
key.description: Show the transport and codecs under the active device while casting

key.name: indicator-location
key.description: Where to show the cast indicator: the top-bar tray, or the quick settings menu.
